9. Manufacture and service economics

The economic model uses:

Production quantity 100 for repeat manufacture.
Twenty-year financial horizon.
8% real discount rate.
5,000 prospective exchanges/year.
90% useful availability.
Electricity at $80/MWh.
Finite replacement intervals and explicit shared-factory labor allocation.
Capital
Item	Allowance
Repeat-installed machine	$211,150
First build, engineering, fitting and initial validation provisions	$494,766
Ordinary industrial working stock, separately reported	$14,000

The repeat bill includes the cradle and anchors, six pods, twelve force channels, six pose heads, gantry, reacted torque tool, cutter, cages, racks, cleaning, interfaces, guards, controls, manufacturing yield, assembly and installation.

The apparent reduction from the previous service-cost construction depends substantially on reusing inspected connection kits instead of consuming a precision set on every healthy cycle. The introduced 500-use kit life remains a life assumption. A 500-exchange campaign circulating sixteen kits does not demonstrate 500 uses of each kit.

Matched comparisons
Route	Conditional cost per exchange	Operational human work/year
Candidate	$11.64	61.93 h
Strong assisted implementation	$16.08	476.40 h
Automated adopter with the same useful primitive	$11.64	61.93 h
Favorable adopter with 25% lower installed capital	$10.51	Same assumed service work

The assisted case gets the same good interfaces, shoring, evidence and escape route. Its introduced active human exchange work is five minutes, not a deliberately slow manual procedure.

Commercial competitors are substantial. ATI lists the QC-76 with separate static moment capacities of 542 Nm and 701 Nm; those values do not establish every simultaneous load combination. STARK distinguishes precision-preserving insertion force from overload retention after its zero point has been left, and specifies finite operating and maintenance conditions. A competent comparator should receive those capabilities and appropriate fixtures.
